healthcareSystem: Excellent universal healthcare system funded by mandatory social insurance. EU/EEA citizens covered with EHIC. One of the best-funded healthcare systems in Europe.
qualityNotes: Outstanding healthcare quality. Modern facilities. Most medical staff speak multiple languages (French, German, English, Luxembourgish). Short wait times compared to neighboring countries.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open Mon-Fri 8am-6:30pm, Sat 8am-12:30pm. Duty pharmacies cover nights, weekends, and holidays.
pharmacyTips: Green cross marks pharmacies. Pharmacists speak multiple languages. Well-stocked pharmacies with high standards. Check the duty pharmacy schedule (pharmacie de garde) for after-hours needs.
prescriptionRules: Follows EU prescription regulations strictly. Many medications require a prescription. EU/EEA prescriptions accepted.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Luxembourg legalized personal cannabis cultivation and use in 2023. CBD products must meet EU regulations.

bringDocumentation: EU/EEA travelers carry a Schengen certificate. Non-EU travelers need a doctor's letter. Keep medications in original packaging.

travelInsurance.tips: Luxembourg has excellent but expensive healthcare. Insurance is strongly recommended for non-EU visitors.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory or specially recommended vaccinations. Luxembourg is a very low-risk destination. Ensure routine vaccinations are current.

waterNotes: Tap water is excellent quality and safe to drink everywhere in Luxembourg.
foodSafetyTips: Excellent food safety standards. Diverse culinary scene reflecting French, German, and international influences. All food establishments maintain high hygiene standards.
medicalTourismNote: Luxembourg is not a typical medical tourism destination due to high costs, but offers exceptional quality for those who seek it.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Luxembourg. Emergency number 112, pharmacy tips, hospital info, and travel insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Centre Hospitalier de Luxembourg (CHL)
hospitals.notes: Main hospital. Full emergency services 24/7. Multilingual staff (French, German, English, Luxembourgish).

hospitals.name: Hôpitaux Robert Schuman (HRS)
hospitals.notes: Major hospital group. Modern facilities near the European institutions area.

hospitals.name: Centre Hospitalier du Nord (CHdN)
hospitals.notes: Main hospital for northern Luxembourg and the Ardennes tourist region.

dentalCare.availability: Excellent dental care. Multilingual dentists throughout the country.
dentalCare.costRange: €50-120 for consultation; €80-250 for fillings; €100-300 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: High-quality dental care but expensive. Most dentists speak French, German, and English.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Call CHL (Centre Hospitalier de Luxembourg) for dental emergencies outside regular hours.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Available. Luxembourg's international population means many therapists speak English. Expect €80-120 per session.
mentalHealth.notes: Good mental health services in multiple languages. Large international community means English-speaking options are common.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Good accessibility infrastructure. Luxembourg has invested in accessible public spaces and transport.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: All hospitals are wheelchair accessible with modern facilities.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Luxembourg has free public transport since 2020. Buses and trams are wheelchair accessible. The modern tram system is fully accessible.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Luxembourg City's Grund (lower town) is accessed by elevator. The Kirchberg district is modern and accessible. Historical old town has some cobblestone areas.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Tests available at pharmacies and clinics.
covidStatus.notes: Luxembourg has lifted all COVID restrictions.

insuranceClaimProcess: Luxembourg hospitals provide detailed multilingual documentation. EU/EEA citizens present EHIC. Non-EU visitors pay upfront and claim from insurance. Healthcare costs are high — keep all receipts.
